rubric.role_summary: Senior engineer responsible for the design, development, testing, and integration of in-space propulsion systems for satellites, including propulsion-system trades and cross-disciplinary technical leadership.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Senior engineer responsible for the design, development, testing, and integration of in-space propulsion systems for satellites, including propulsion-system trades and cross-disciplinary technical leadership.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Space Systems, or Electrical Engineering, or an equivalent Engineering or Applied Physics degree.
- 5 years of experience identifying, designing, developing and/or building satellite or RCS propulsion solutions.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- 10 years of experience with satellite and/or RCS propulsion systems, including electric and chemical propulsion.
- Systems-level experience deriving propulsion requirements for various satellite applications.
- Experience managing external suppliers and internal development efforts in parallel.
- Physics-based component design experience for performance and manufacturability.
- Advanced degree in a relevant engineering discipline.
- Experience incorporating test or operational data into thruster continuous improvement efforts.
- Experience throughout the whole product lifecycle, balancing design, analytical performance, manufacturing, operation, and business constraints.
- Team and/or software project management experience.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Accept any one of these geographic alternatives (OR): Greater Seattle, Washington area (onsite; metadata lists Kent, Washington). Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them. Onsite work is based in one of these areas. Relocation is offered; candidates outside these areas may qualify with explicit evidence of willingness to relocate. Current residence in the area is not mandatory.
